clue.text: Pirate also on the vessel

parts.note: a brig is a two-masted sailing ship
and means also, in addition

explanation.surface: A buccaneer is aboard the ship too.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigand is a bandit or robber, and a pirate is a robber at sea.

clue.text: Live teams as well

parts.note: to be is to exist or live
sides are opposing teams in a game

explanation.surface: Broadcasting the teams live, as well as everything else.
explanation.definitionFit: Besides is an adverb meaning in addition, too.

clue.text: Colder reception of monarch by chemical company

parts.note: ICI was Imperial Chemical Industries, the British chemical giant
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A chemical firm gave the visiting monarch a frosty welcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reception of monarch by' means ICI takes in the monarch at its end, so ER follows ICI.
explanation.definitionFit: Icier is the comparative of icy, meaning more freezing.

clue.text: Sailor holds marks — or will not do so

parts.note: AB is an able seaman
stains are marks or blemishes

explanation.surface: A sailor takes on stains, or else refuses to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holds' here just joins the sailor to the marks he carries.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who abstains deliberately refrains from an action, so will not do it.

clue.text: Party award after death

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration
OM is the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A celebration and an honour come after someone dies.
explanation.definitionFit: Doom means fate, especially ruin or death.

clue.text: Piece of land or farming aid

parts.note: a tract is an area of land

explanation.surface: A plot of ground or a piece of agricultural kit.
explanation.definitionFit: A tractor is the vehicle that pulls ploughs and other implements on a farm.

clue.text: Gnashing teeth, I clap this form of communication

indicators.note: gnashing grinds and churns things up, so these letters are ground into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone grinding teeth and clapping as a way of making themselves understood.
explanation.definitionFit: Telepathic contact is mind-to-mind transfer of thoughts without speech.

clue.text: Come to a sober conclusion

parts.note: TT means teetotal, never drinking alcohol
an end is a conclusion

explanation.surface: Reaching a clear-headed decision.
explanation.definitionFit: To attend an event is to be present at it, to turn up there.

clue.text: Far too wet to go out? We could try this

indicators.note: letters that go out are scattered from their places, signalling these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: It is too rainy to leave the house, so we might stay in with a cuppa.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an indoor pastime for a wet day; a pot of tea shared by two fits the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: A pot of tea for a pair is the sort of cosy thing to have on a rainy afternoon.

clue.text: Side at loose end sat for the photographer, then rested

parts.note: R is right, one side

indicators.note: the end of the word loose is its final letter

parts.note: a model who sat for a photographer posed

explanation.surface: Someone at a loose end modelled for a camera and then had a lie-down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loose end' looks like an idiom for being idle but gives the last letter of 'loose'.
explanation.definitionFit: Reposed means lay at rest, relaxed.

clue.text: National registry for food

parts.note: a Swiss national is a citizen of Switzerland
a roll is a register or official list of names

explanation.surface: A country's official records being used as something to eat.
explanation.definitionFit: A Swiss roll is a sponge cake spread with jam and rolled up.

clue.text: Wallowing in gin — male vagrant

indicators.note: the male wallows inside the snare, so his letter sits within the other word

parts.note: a gin is a snare or trap for game

explanation.surface: A man soaking himself in gin, a down-and-out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gin' looks like the drink but is the snare.
explanation.definitionFit: A tramp is a homeless wanderer, a vagrant.

clue.text: A rod in pickle for him

indicators.note: to be in a pickle is to be in a mess, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone has a rod in pickle for him: a punishment stored up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A rod in pickle' is an old idiom for a punishment stored up for someone; here A ROD IN is the fodder and 'pickle' the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Dorian is a man's name, as in Wilde's Dorian Gray, so it can stand for a male person.

clue.text: Impoverished Poles held captive in vessel? Supporters called for!

indicators.note: the whole captive group goes in the ship, inside its letters

parts.note: SS is a steamship

indicators.note: the poles are held captive inside the word for poor, so they sit within it

parts.note: poor means impoverished
N and S are the north and south poles

explanation.surface: Penniless Poles locked in a ship call for help from backers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poles' looks like people from Poland but is the two magnetic poles.
explanation.definitionFit: Sponsors are backers who fund or support a cause.

clue.text: Skilled in diplomacy — yet can make Arabs so mad

definitions.note: an adjectival phrase standing for a noun: the one skilled in diplomacy

indicators.note: these words can make something else when rearranged, signalling a reshuffle

explanation.surface: A skilful diplomat could still enrage Arabs.
explanation.definitionFit: An envoy representing a state abroad is a person skilled in diplomacy.

clue.text: Another success on board for the officer

parts.note: a second is another one
mate is the winning move in chess, played on a board

explanation.surface: A further triumph on ship for an officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on board' suggests aboard ship, but it is the chessboard.
explanation.definitionFit: A second mate is a ship's officer ranking below the first mate.

clue.text: With fish go in for chips

parts.note: carp is a freshwater fish
to enter is to go in

explanation.surface: Fish with chips on the side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chips' is the traditional nickname for a carpenter, from wood chips, not fried potatoes.
explanation.definitionFit: Chips was the old naval nickname for a ship's woodworker.

clue.text: Horses kicking dust around

indicators.note: kicking the dust around throws its letters into disorder

explanation.surface: Horses kick up dust all around them.
explanation.definitionFit: A stud is an establishment of horses kept for breeding.

clue.text: Learned coin should be dropped in rising river

indicators.note: the coin is dropped into the river, so its letters go inside
in a down clue rising means the word is read upwards, backwards

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Britain
a ducat is an old gold coin

explanation.surface: A coin ought to be thrown into a river in flood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' turns DEE into EED, into which DUCAT drops.
explanation.definitionFit: Educated means schooled and learned.

clue.text: This bird left Noah's boat

parts.note: the ark is the vessel Noah built for the flood

explanation.surface: This bird flew from Noah's vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A lark is a songbird such as the skylark.

clue.text: A free hand needed to hold a dog

explanation.surface: You need a free hand to hold a dog's lead.
explanation.definitionFit: A licence is a freedom to act as one likes, and a dog licence was once required in Britain to keep a dog.

clue.text: Figure there's a crony in the hangar

parts.note: a pal is a crony or friend
drome is short for aerodrome, where aircraft are housed

explanation.surface: A man's friend is spotted in the aircraft shed.
explanation.definitionFit: A number such as 1881 reads the same both ways, so it is a symmetrical figure.

clue.text: Turning pale to begin with, slipped away

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held, 'Turning pale to begin with, slipped away (7)': an anagram of PALE gives ELAP but nothing in the clue supplies SED; a word appears to be missing or misread
annotationWithheld.clue: Turning pale to begin with, slipped away

clue.text: Sound of word changed when hand is crooked

indicators.note: something crooked is bent out of shape, so these letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: A word's sound alters when a hand is bent.
explanation.definitionFit: In linguistics sandhi is the change in a word's sound caused by its neighbours.

clue.text: Cavers change direction, reaching this rift

indicators.note: change tells us to alter the order of these letters

parts.note: SE is south-east, a compass direction

explanation.surface: Potholers alter course on reaching a crack in the ice.
explanation.definitionFit: A crevasse is a deep crack in a glacier.

clue.text: Plant an espionage bureau at the back of athletic club

indicators.note: the espionage words come behind the club, following it

parts.note: an gives the single letter A
the CIA is the US Central Intelligence Agency

explanation.surface: Planting a spy agency behind a sports club.
explanation.definitionFit: An acacia is a tree or shrub such as the wattle.

clue.text: Get over without being spotted

explanation.surface: Escape across a border unseen.
explanation.definitionFit: To clear a fence is to get over it, and clear skin is free of spots.

clue.text: Loud sort of game on board

indicators.note: sort means put in order, so the letters are sorted afresh

explanation.surface: A noisy board game.
explanation.definitionFit: Ludo is a children's board game played with dice and counters.

clue.text: Bright return for vessel I'd found

indicators.note: return means the word is turned back to front

parts.note: a tin is a container or vessel

explanation.surface: A good result after finding a container.
explanation.definitionFit: Nitid is a literary word for shining or lustrous.

clue.text: Indubitably it's good advice for the pessimist

explanation.surface: Surely a gloomy person should be told to worry less.
explanation.definitionFit: Doubtless means certainly; split in two it urges a pessimist to have fewer misgivings.

clue.text: Before now, first person to intervene between nobleman and monarch

parts.note: an earl is a nobleman
I is the first person pronoun
ER is Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: Someone comes between a lord and the Queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to intervene between' places I between the nobleman and the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Earlier means at a previous time, before the present.

clue.text: Requested to be methodical

explanation.surface: Asked to be orderly.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordered means asked for or commanded, and also tidy and systematic.
